title: Tile a watermark across a PNG

seo.metaTitle: Watermark Tile PNG - Free Browser Tool, No Upload Needed
seo.metaDescription: Cover a picture with a repeating diagonal text watermark: set the wording, angle, spacing and opacity. Runs locally, free, nothing leaves the device.
seo.longDescription: Tile a watermark across a PNG covers the whole picture with the same short text repeated in a diagonal grid — the usual way to mark a draft, a proof or a preview so it is not mistaken for a finished file. Type the text (DRAFT, SAMPLE, a site name) and shape the pattern: Angle tilts it from -90 to 90 degrees, Step X and Step Y set how far apart the repeats sit, Opacity decides how firmly the lettering shows through; the defaults give a diagonal grid at thirty percent. The lettering is rendered by the browser with the fonts on your device, so the picture is never uploaded.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Repeats cover the whole frame — there is no corner to crop away.
Angle from -90 to 90 degrees; Step X and Step Y control the density of the grid.
Burned into the pixels: the downloaded file looks the same everywhere.
Free with no daily limit and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Type the watermark text - a single word such as DRAFT is usually enough.
Tilt the grid with Angle, then set Step X and Step Y to space out the repeats.
Lower Opacity until the text stays readable without fighting the picture, then download.

faq.q: Should I use this or the add text tool?
faq.a: Add text draws a single label in one of nine positions, which suits a caption or a signature. This one repeats across the whole frame, which suits protection - there is no corner to crop away.

faq.q: Why does the watermark look denser in some places?
faq.a: That is the geometry of the grid. Step X and Step Y define one repeat per cell, and at the default spacing the word is wider than its cell, so neighbouring rows touch. Raise the steps until clear gaps open up.
Yes. Angle 0 draws the repeats upright along the axes, while 30 to 45 degrees gives the slanted look usually used for a watermark.

faq.q: Is the watermark burned into the file?
faq.a: Yes - the repeats are drawn into the pixels, so a downloaded file looks the same everywhere. The font itself comes from this device, which is why an identical setting can render a little differently on another machine.
